text:
Samir: RFC drop — proposing a hybrid "seed-first + index bloom" sync for air-gapped upgrades. want quick eyes on security/rollback tradeoffs.
Marco: skimmed. high level sounds promising to reduce seed size. do you have numbers? :thinking: 
Samir: rough numbers: for a 500GB bundle, full seed can be 20GB. with bloom filters for chunk index + dedupe we can drop to ~600MB seed. rebuild still needs streaming the rest.
Tess: can we guarantee monotonic apply ordering? rollback scenarios worry me.
Samir: plan is two-phase: seed (signed, small) then incremental chunk stream with signed segment manifests. apply only after segment signatures verified and activation window cleared.
Elaine: how do we handle false positives from bloom? could cause us to skip needed chunks.
Samir: bloom is only used to decide which chunk hashes to request in phase 2. false positives => we request a chunk we already have, small extra cost. false negatives are impossible if we set filters correctly (we'll use counting bloom variant and explicit metadata for critical files).
Nate: counting bloom adds memory. devices in field may be low-RAM.
Samir: agreed, fallback to compact index for low-memory targets. we detect device capability in handshake.
deploy-bot: deploy note: this will change bootstrap handshake payload (seed-version + bloom-v1|compact), rollout needs console flag.
Marco: signing: are we signing the bloom/filter bundle? who rotates keys? security?
security: we should sign seed + bloom metadata together with ks://redwood-bootstrap-v1 sig. keys rotated monthly via operator flow. include key-id and sig in manifest.
Elaine: activation window problem: if a partial stream is applied and then interrupted, we need safe rollback with proof-of-activation.
Samir: idea: keep apply journal with seq numbers + segment merkle root. activation is committing a final manifest that references applied merkle roots and is signed. revert by replaying journal until last committed seq.
Tess: journal growth might be big. can we checkpoint and prune older entries?
Samir: yes — checkpoint every N segments and tombstone earlier entries after a snapshot signature. snapshot also signed.
Nate: compatibility: older agents will only support seed-first full bundle. we need graceful downgrade.
Samir: handshake includes supported-modes list. when contacting seed-server, agent advertises supported-modes. server picks compatible flow.
Elaine: curious about privacy — bloom could leak presence of files across devices if intercepted.
security: bloom metadata signed but not encrypted. for high-sensitivity deployments we'll offer encrypted seed channel using customer KMS; bloom can be encrypted symmetrically as well.
Marco: show me a minimal manifest example of segment header.
Samir: paste:

```
segment: 42
seq_start: 1001
seq_end: 1200
merkle_root: sha256:ab12...
bloom: bloom:v1:sha256:ff33... size:8M fp:0.01
sig: ks://redwood-bootstrap-v1:SIGBASE64
```

Tess: looks fine. how about network backpressure? large deployments will have many agents clamoring for stream.
Samir: we plan server-side rate limiting + per-agent reactive backoff. stream supports sparse-resume by seq range.
deploy-bot: reminder: change will be required in onprem installer and console agent config.
Elaine: ops playbook for failed activation?
Samir: steps: 1) check journal and last snapshot 2) attempt sparse-resume from seq+1 3) if corruption, mark device quarantined and provide rollback bundle (signed) with explicit revert manifest.
Nate: what about disk space during apply — we temporarily need both old and new copies for atomic swap.
Samir: we use two-phase swap with file-level renames where possible and preallocate segment caches; fallback to copy-on-write for FS without atomic rename.
Marco: ok, next actions?
Samir: draft RFC link: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/hybrid-seed-bloom (WIP). need security review (assigned), ops to validate playbook steps on lab hardware, eng-infra to add handshake fields. I'll send changes by EOD.
Elaine: assign to me for ops testing.
security: will schedule review for key rotation and KMS integration.
Marco: SGTM. :thumbsup:
